title: How digoxin and other inotropes strengthen the heartbeat
ariaLabel: Schematic of cardiac contractility: the sodium-potassium pump keeps intracellular sodium low, which lets the heart cell push calcium out, beta-1 receptor signalling raises cAMP, and phosphodiesterase 3 breaks cAMP down. Digoxin blocks the sodium-potassium pump so calcium stays in and contraction is stronger, beta-1 agonists such as dobutamine raise cAMP, and milrinone blocks phosphodiesterase 3.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

nodes.label: Sodium-potassium pump
nodes.info: The pump that keeps sodium low inside heart cells.

nodes.label: Calcium pushed out
nodes.info: Calcium removed from the cell by the exchanger when the pump works normally.

nodes.label: Beta-1 signal
nodes.info: Beta-1 receptor stimulation on heart cells.

nodes.label: cAMP made
nodes.info: cAMP raises calcium entry and contraction.

nodes.label: cAMP breakdown
nodes.info: Phosphodiesterase 3 breaks cAMP down in heart and vessels.

nodes.label: Contractility
nodes.info: A teaching score for the strength of the heart cell's contraction.

edges.label: Na/K ATPase
edges.info: Digoxin blocks the pump, so sodium rises inside the cell, the sodium-calcium exchanger pushes less calcium out, and more calcium is stored and released with each beat.
More calcium pushed out lowers contraction.

edges.label: beta-1 and cAMP
edges.info: Beta-1 agonists (dobutamine) raise cAMP, which opens calcium channels and strengthens contraction.

edges.label: PDE3
edges.info: Milrinone blocks PDE3, so cAMP lasts longer. It also widens vessels.

sources: Where each class acts. Digoxin blocks the sodium-potassium pump so more calcium is stored, beta-1 agonists raise cAMP, and milrinone blocks phosphodiesterase 3. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Heart failure drugs that improve survival (shown in the beta-blocker, RAAS and diuretic figures), digoxin effects on rhythm and the vagus, toxicity and levels, potassium interactions, vasopressors, levosimendan, dose and monitoring are left out. Contractility is drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
